content.text: The one validation test failed. I'm stopping the search there and submitting that portfolio as is.

I submitted an equal-weighted short-term reversal portfolio: it trades all 94 one-month momentum signals (ma_5_21 and tsmom_21 for each of the 47 industries) in reverse. Its training Sharpe is 0.40 (1970–1999), but it **failed** its only validation test (2000–2012), so I expect its Sharpe on unseen data to be close to zero.

I used just 1 of the 200 backtest calls, on purpose. Individual signals don't hold up: the correlation between their Sharpes in the first and second halves of the training period is −0.03. Only 30 of the 423 signals are statistically significant, about what chance alone would produce (~19). If I had kept tweaking portfolios until one passed, that pass would probably have been luck and wouldn't carry over to 2013 onward. So I submitted the one candidate that has a clear economic reason behind it and holds up across the whole data set, even though it failed validation.
